verification_method: Primary pages opened and relevant passages checked in this run; candidate metadata APIs fetched directly.
scope_note: References justify design choices and data interpretation. Implemented scope and final cohort are defined by executed code and generated manifests.
version_note: Stable scikit-learn documentation is dynamic; use the installed software version recorded by the project when reproducing code.

sources.application: Define the data grain, outcome, date parsing, measurement audit and frozen-source manifest.
sources.title: NCBI Pathogen Detection AST Browser Documentation
supports: One row is one submitted experimental AST result, usually with multiple results per isolate.
Phenotypes are submitter-reported, distinct from genotype predictions.
MIC and disk diffusion fields use different units; comparison signs and combination concentrations must be retained.
Collection dates may be missing, partial, or years earlier than submission; database updates daily.

sources.application: Validate and normalize values while preserving nonbinary and censored semantics.
sources.title: NCBI BioSample Antibiograms
supports: Controlled phenotype vocabulary includes R, S, I, NS, not defined and susceptible-dose dependent.
Comparison operators distinguish exact measurements from upper/lower bounds.
Combination measurements have number1/number2 format.
MIC units include mg/L and equivalent micrograms/mL; disk diffusion uses mm.
Documented value ranges are positive up to 1024 for mg/L and 6 through 150 for mm.

sources.application: State provenance, quality-control limits and selection bias.
sources.title: NCBI Antibiotic Susceptibility Test Browser
supports: AST results are submitted through BioSample.
NCBI does not comprehensively vet supplied testing methods and values.
Collection differences limit interpretation of overall resistance frequencies.

sources.application: Join accessions explicitly and freeze source files, queries, timestamps and checksums.
sources.title: NCBI Pathogen Detection Help
supports: Isolate records link BioSample, BioProject, metadata, AMR genotypes and AST phenotypes.
Resources are updated approximately daily; indexing or cloud synchronization can lag.
AMR genotype calls and AST phenotypes are distinct indexed fields.

sources.application: Treat gene calls as predictors and retain independent experimental outcomes; qualify negative calls.
sources.title: Interpreting AMRFinderPlus results
supports: Presence of an AMR gene or mutation does not necessarily establish phenotypic resistance.
AMRFinderPlus does not itself predict phenotypic resistance.
Unreported point mutations are not proof of their absence.

sources.application: Identify the origin and scope of genomic annotations.
sources.title: NCBI AMRFinderPlus
supports: AMRFinderPlus identifies AMR genes, resistance-associated point mutations and selected other gene classes using assembled sequence or protein annotations.

sources.application: Document candidate comparison; no executed analyses are attributed to inaccessible data files.
sources.title: ARMD-UTSW: deidentified electronic health records for antimicrobial resistance research
supports: Clinical EHR alternative includes culture, demographic, laboratory, prior-resistance and history tables.
Public dataset metadata reports CC0 and 237258 patients.

sources.application: Record exact candidate version and access audit.
sources.title: ARMD-UTSW current dataset metadata API
supports: Version link resolves to /api/v2/versions/398029 at audit time.
License resolves to CC0-1.0.

sources.application: Keep related isolate/study/cluster observations together and audit each fold.
sources.title: scikit-learn StratifiedGroupKFold
supports: Cross-validation preserves non-overlapping groups while attempting class balance.
Perfect stratification is not guaranteed when group structure constrains it.

sources.application: Export explicit phenotype-target mappings; avoid arbitrary feature ranks in linear models.
sources.title: scikit-learn LabelEncoder
supports: LabelEncoder is for target y rather than feature matrix X.
Classes and numeric labels can be recovered through the fitted class mapping.

sources.application: Make fitted feature-label mappings and missing/unseen policies reviewable.
sources.title: scikit-learn OrdinalEncoder
supports: Categorical features can use integer codes with distinct missing and unseen-category handling.
Automatic categories are learned from training data.

sources.application: Represent nominal categories without imposing a numeric order; reduce sparse rare categories using development data.
sources.title: scikit-learn OneHotEncoder
supports: One-hot encoding supports unknown-category handling and training-frequency-based rare categories.

sources.application: Compare justified imputation alternatives and preserve missingness information; do not call a single run multiple imputation.
sources.title: scikit-learn Imputation of missing values
supports: Simple, neighbor-based and iterative approaches are available with missingness indicators.
IterativeImputer is experimental and returns one completed matrix per run by default.
Repeated posterior-sampling runs can support multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses.

sources.application: Fit calibration only within development splits and evaluate held-out probability quality.
sources.title: scikit-learn Probability calibration
supports: Calibration maps classifier outputs to observed probability frequencies.
Calibration data must be separate from data used to fit the classifier.
Reliability diagrams and proper scoring rules help assess probabilities.

sources.application: Keep vocabulary, frequency thresholds, imputation and feature selection inside training partitions.
sources.title: scikit-learn Common pitfalls and recommended practices
supports: Split data before fitting learned preprocessing.
Fit and fit_transform must exclude test data.
Pipelines apply preprocessing consistently and reduce leakage during model selection.

sources.title: Feldgarden et al. (2021). AMRFinderPlus and the Reference Gene Catalog facilitate examination of the genomic links among antimicrobial resistance, stress response, and virulence. Scientific Reports 11:12728.
supports: Curated genomic annotations have evidence categories and do not constitute de novo resistance discovery.

sources.title: Yu, Wheeler and Barquist (2025). Biased sampling driven by bacterial population structure confounds machine learning prediction of antimicrobial resistance. PLOS Biology23:e3003539.
supports: Population structure and biased sampling can confound AMR prediction; more samples alone need not resolve the problem.
